doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Opening: medicine, music and baseball as Budd's three interests
summary: Rowe introduces Budd, his age and his three main interests, and suggests starting there.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: Today we’re filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive in Aspen, Colorado, and I’m very happy to have Dr. John Budd, man of medicine and a jazz fan with a capital F — I think that’s safe to say.
In the little bit I’ve talked to you, I have actually learned that I don’t know nearly as much as I thought I did.
My. Isn’t that part of learning?
Yes I think so. Because your appreciation of the music seems to go way back. You are going to celebrate your 89th birthday in February is that correct?
Thank you. It’s well to do it in advance at my age. Don’t jump too far ahead. Prophecy is dangerous.
Right. Well you have said to me a couple of times that your three main interests in your life have been medicine, music and baseball.
And that they are not so far apart as we might tend to think.
Is that a place where we could start talking?
